thought: The external search supports the GDPR legal-obligation exception, and the policy output identifies exactly which categories our rules retain. Invoices are not listed as a retained category, so I should distinguish the general GDPR position from this rule set.
input:
Generally, yes—but not merely because an invoice exists. GDPR Article 17(3)(b) permits an exception to erasure where processing is necessary to comply with a legal obligation. Applicable tax or accounting rules may require invoices to be retained. The company should retain only what is required, for the required period, and limit further use and access. This is general background from the external search, not case-specific advice.

That only partly matches our rules. They retain security audit logs during their supplied retention period, legal-hold records while a supplied hold is active, and backup archives when restore access can be blocked. Invoices are not a category named in the rules, so the rule set does not itself establish an invoice-retention exception. An invoice would need to be covered by an applicable legal obligation and the relevant policy/rules would need to address its treatment.
